Start with a question about differential gene expression. Learn a complete workflow using fictional counts, repeat it using real airway data, and then adapt it to your study. Check inputs, verify outputs, and explain what the analysis can establish.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## One workflow for every dataset

1. **Define the question** and contrast.
2. **Preview the results** you will produce.
3. **Meet the inputs** and understand their structure.
4. **Check the inputs** and design.
5. **Run the analysis** using a documented command.
6. **Verify and explain** tables, figures, and limitations.
7. **Write the report** with evidence and limitations.
:::

| Dataset | Input | Main learning goal |
|---|---|---|
| [Synthetic practice](examples/synthetic/00-start-here.qmd) | Fictional integer gene counts, six samples per group | Learn checks, DESeq2 outputs, and independent sample verification |
| [Airway case study](examples/airway/00-start-here.qmd) | Gene counts from four cell lines measured untreated and treated | Include cell line in the design and interpret a real experiment |
| [Your own study](examples/my-study/00-start-here.qmd) | Your count matrix and study metadata | Check design and adapt the workflow responsibly |

This guide starts with **gene-level count tables**. It does not process FASTQ reads, align sequences, or quantify transcripts. Differential expression describes an association with the specified contrast under the chosen design; it does not alone establish causation outside the experiment or clinical benefit.
